holidays.name: National Weatherperson's Day
holidays.description: A day to thank the meteorologists who brave the wrath of unpredictable skies, and who get blamed when the picnic gets rained out. Weather nerds celebrate by checking radar maps and admiring cloud formations.
holidays.origin: Observed in the United States on February 5 to honor the birthday of John Jeffries, born in 1745, an early American weather observer who took some of the first recorded weather observations in the country.
holidays.funFact: John Jeffries made some of the earliest weather observations in America and also took weather readings from a hot air balloon over the English Channel in 1785.

holidays.name: World Nutella Day
holidays.description: A global celebration of the chocolate hazelnut spread that has rescued countless slices of toast and spoons at midnight. Fans share recipes, photos, and questionable spoonful-straight-from-the-jar confessions.
holidays.origin: Started in 2007 by bloggers Sara Rosso and Michelle Fabio as a fan-created tribute to Nutella. Ferrero, the maker of Nutella, later took over the observance.
holidays.funFact: Nutella was born from wartime shortage: the Italian pastry maker Pietro Ferrero stretched scarce chocolate by mixing in hazelnuts, which were plentiful in Piedmont.

holidays.name: National Shower With a Friend Day
holidays.description: A tongue-in-cheek observance that is mostly about saving water, though it mainly gets people raising eyebrows and making jokes. Participants are encouraged to take shorter showers and conserve resources.
holidays.origin: An unofficial, internet-era observance that spread through novelty holiday calendars, with a nominal environmental angle focused on water conservation.
holidays.funFact: The average American shower uses roughly 17 gallons of water, so cutting shower time even by a couple of minutes adds up to big savings over a year.

holidays.name: National Chocolate Fondue Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to dipping strawberries, marshmallows, pretzels, and anything else within reach into a pot of molten chocolate. It is the one day when double-dipping at a party is entirely forgiven.
holidays.origin: An unofficial food holiday that fits neatly between the Super Bowl season and Valentine's Day, encouraging cozy dessert gatherings. Fondue itself traces back to Switzerland, where it began as a cheese dish.
holidays.funFact: Chocolate fondue was popularized in the 1960s in New York City, when a Swiss restaurateur named Konrad Egli created it as a promotional dessert for his Chalet Suisse restaurant.

holidays.name: Disaster Day
holidays.description: A day of sheer shenanigans in which you celebrate things going gloriously wrong, and laugh at burnt dinners and spilled coffee. It is a reminder that mishaps make for the best stories.
holidays.origin: A lighthearted unofficial observance on novelty holiday calendars, meant to encourage people to embrace imperfection and have a sense of humor about mistakes.
holidays.funFact: Many famous inventions, including the microwave oven and Post-it notes, came from happy accidents, so your disaster might be the start of something great.
